craft_evidence.owned: Workshop in Victoria, BC described by the brand as "the Viberg workshop"; third-generation family-owned company (brand claim only; no filing, photo or tour read by me; ownership of the premises not stated on the brand pages read)
craft_evidence.makers: NONE (no named individual makers/workshops on the 9 product pages read beyond Viberg itself)
craft_evidence.mills: Tanneries named in the brand journal, not on product pages read: Horween Leather Company (Shell Cordovan, "working closely" 10+ years) and Shinki (Horsebutt). Chromexcel(R) named on product titles without tannery. Rocky Mountain not found.
craft_evidence.madein: 3 of 9 product pages read state Made in Canada (145 Oxford, Hiker, Outsider II); the other 6 are silent; journal says boots "continue to be made in Victoria"
craft_evidence.heritage: Dated and placed: founded 1931; Edwin moved from Saskatchewan to BC and settled in Victoria; 3rd generation; Service Boot first introduced 1931
craft_evidence.process: Yes: /pages/process describes Channelled Insole Goodyear Welt and Stitchdown (hand-skived upper, vamp turned outward, 4.8-5mm midsole, double-row stitch); goodyear first produced late 1960s
craft_evidence.reasoning: Brand describes its own Victoria BC workshop making the footwear (craftsmanship page), family-run since 1931 (journal), with documented Goodyear welt and stitchdown process and named tanneries (Horween, Shinki) in the journal. Held short of certain: ownership of the premises is implied not stated, and Made in Canada appears on only 3 of 9 product pages. Medium confidence; a 4 if Sebastian wants a filing or tour first. Sharp Magazine 2016 factory tour and Montecristo 2019 not read.
